records.title: Affordable Multifamily Program Upstate
records.description: Provides technical assistance and financial incentives to support retrofits in low-to moderate-income (LMI) multifamily buildings in upstate New York under the LMI Energy Efficiency and Building Electrification (EE/BE) Order from 2026-2030.

records.title: Affordable Solar and Storage Predevelopment and Technical Assistance
records.description: Affordable Solar and Storage Predevelopment and Technical Assistance will provide grants to address barriers for solar and/or storage installations serving low-to-moderate income (LMI) households living in rental housing, multifamily buildings, or other households not served by traditional onsite residential solar/storage. Individual awards will not exceed $200,000. Funding to proposals through this solicitation will offset costs for predevelopment and technical assistance work needed to implement solar and/or storage installations for multifamily affordable housing and/or shared solar (Community Distributed Generation) installations that benefit LMI households.

records.title: Appliance Upgrade Program- Application for Retailer and Contractor Enrollment
records.description: Seeks to establish a network of Participating Retailers and Contractors, as part of the Appliance Upgrade Program, to sell (retailers) and install (contractors) ENERGY STAR® certified heat pump dryers (including all-in-one washer-dryers with a heat pump dryer). The Appliance Upgrade Program will provide New York households below the 150% AMI (State’s Area Median Income) with rebates for these appliances and electrical wiring and panel upgrade installations required by such appliance installations.

records.title: Apprenticeship and Pre-apprenticeship Clean Energy Training
records.close_date_note: Next of 2 future NYSERDA application rounds; later rounds are listed in the details.

deadlines.note: Next of 2 future NYSERDA application rounds; later rounds are listed in the details.

records.description: Through this funding opportunity the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) seeks to work with labor organizations and registered pre-apprenticeship programs across the State, to grow a diverse, equitable, and inclusive pipeline of skilled talent for the clean energy labor market. This solicitation is intended to fund Projects that create and/or expand the capacity of direct entry pre-apprenticeships, registered apprenticeship training programs, and journey worker training programs. All project applicants must be affiliated with bona fide labor organizations. Training initiatives must include clean energy technical training in target areas and hands-on experience for apprentices, and/or journey workers. With this funding NYSERDA hopes to support a pathway to high-quality, family supporting jobs by ensuring that New Yorkers have the skills and qualifications required to meet the demands of a clean energy economy.

records.title: Charge Ready NY 2.0
records.description: Charge Ready NY 2.0 (PON 5367) is an incentive program that provides $3,000 per charging port installed at a workplace or multi-unit dwelling (MUD) location, and $4,000 per charging port installed within a Disadvantaged Community (DAC). Completion of the installation of charging equipment and the provision of appropriate documentation are required. Public and private (for-profit and not-for-profit) entities may participate in the Program.

records.title: Clean Energy Career Pathways Training
records.close_date_note: Next of 8 future NYSERDA application rounds; later rounds are listed in the details.

deadlines.note: Next of 8 future NYSERDA application rounds; later rounds are listed in the details.

records.description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) is seeking proposals for clean energy career pathways projects. These projects must include clean energy technical training as well as career preparation, wraparound services, and job placement support to prepare new workers for entry-level clean energy careers. Projects funded under this solicitation are intended to build or expand training infrastructure and capacity to build an equitable and inclusive pipeline of skilled talent for New York’s clean energy labor market. All training funded under this solicitation must be industry-driven and meet a demonstrated business need.

records.title: Clean Green Schools Initiative
records.description: The P-12 Schools: Clean Green Schools Initiative is available to help public schools that traditionally lack resources to invest in infrastructure improvements become healthier, more productive learning environments. The program provides funding for schools to implement construction projects that decarbonize their building portfolio and enhance extreme heat resilience, such as comprehensive retrofits that impact energy consumption and overall building load, electrification readiness projects, and conversion of central heating and/or cooling plants to clean energy technologies such as heat pumps. Schools participating in the program may also receive funding to support eligible activities that create or further clean energy educational opportunities for students, faculty, staff, and the surrounding community.

records.title: Empire Building Challenge: Hospitals
records.description: Through this competitive solicitation, eligible hospitals can request up to $5 million for the construction and installation of scalable, efficient, low-carbon solutions such as electrification of building systems, electrification readiness projects, and comprehensive energy efficiency projects that will achieve significant carbon and/or energy reduction.

records.title: FlexTech Program
records.description: The Flexible Technical Assistance (FlexTech) Program supports New York State commercial, industrial, institutional, and multifamily customers who pay into the Systems Benefit Charge by providing a cost-share for credible, objective technical assistance services, such as energy audits, that help businesses make more informed energy decisions.

records.title: Grid Modernization Grid Enhancing Technologies
records.description: Helping to achieve a modernized energy grid, investments in Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs) roll up to meet New York State’s clean energy goals. Up to $3 million per project is available in Program Opportunity Notice (PON) 6149 to promote product developments and demonstrations that work together to advance the transition of New York State’s electric grid to cleaner resources.

records.title: Large Scale Non-drop-in Alternative Fuels Based Resources and Infrastructure
records.description: Supporting the development, scale-up, and demonstration of large-scale alternative fuel-based energy systems and supporting infrastructure, up to $8 million is available through Program Opportunity Notice (PON) 6161. This funding will help advance solutions optimized for safe, cost-effective, and scalable deployment of non-drop-in fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia within New York State. This competitive solicitation, offered through NYSERDA’s Advanced Fuels Program, seeks qualified proposers to design, develop, and validate integrated energy and infrastructure systems.

records.title: Municipal Permitting Modernization Program
records.description: NYSERDA PON 5862 seeks applications from NYS municipalities interested in no-cost access to Citizenserve®, software, a browser-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform for building plan approval (“Program Software”), including a subscription, support, and training for two years. For the purposes of this PON, the term “municipality” refers to cities, towns, villages and counties in New York State.

records.title: New York School Bus Incentive Program
records.description: The New York School Bus Incentive Program (NYSBIP) is a voucher incentive program to accelerate the deployment of zero-emission school buses and associated charging infrastructure throughout New York State using funds allocated by the 2022 Clean Water, Clean Air, and Green Jobs Environmental Bond Act (Bond Act). More information about how fleets, dealers, and manufacturers can participate in NYSBIP can be found at the NYSBIP website.

records.title: New York State Clean Energy Internship Program
records.description: Provides funding to eligible clean energy businesses, organizations, and local municipalities hiring interns to perform meaningful work in the clean energy sector. Both clean energy employers and interns can apply to participate in the program. Accepted employers will select, interview, and hire interns, and NYSERDA provides reimbursement on a percentage of the interns’ wages.

records.title: NY-Sun Commercial / Industrial Incentive Program
records.description: The NY-Sun Program provides cash incentives for the installation by Contractors of new grid-connected electric photovoltaic (PV) systems that range from 750kW to 7.5MW in the Upstate region. Incentives are granted on a first-come, first-served basis and PV project applications will be accepted through December 31, 2030, or until funds are fully committed, whichever comes first. Total incentives available are subject to change.

records.title: NY-Sun Residential/Nonresidential Incentive Program
records.description: The NY-Sun Program provides cash incentives for the installation of new grid-connected electric photovoltaic (PV) systems for residential and nonresidential sites completed by Contractors and Builders. Incentives are granted on a first-come, first-served basis, and PV project applications will be accepted through December 31, 2030, or until funds are fully committed, whichever comes first. Total incentives available are subject to change.

records.title: On-site Energy Manager Program
records.description: Offers a cost-share for industrial, commercial, and multifamily facilities or buildings to hire a dedicated, full-time or part-time on-site energy manager. Energy managers are responsible for creating efficient processes that decrease cost and waste—helping organizations lower operational costs, reduce maintenance time, and create comfortable, safe facilities.

records.title: On-the-Job Training for Energy Efficiency and Clean Technology
records.description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) will provide incentives to eligible energy efficiency and clean technology employers to hire and provide on-the-job training for new workers. NYSERDA’s intent for this is to advance the state’s energy goals by developing a workforce equipped to perform jobs in energy efficiency and clean technology.

records.title: Owner's Representative Services for Multifamily Buildings
records.description: The Owner’s Representative Services for Multifamily Buildings Program provides incentives to multifamily owners and managers of under-resourced multifamily buildings, for technical assistance and support services to advance efficiency and decarbonization projects.

records.title: Residential and Retail Energy Storage Market Acceleration Incentives Programs
records.description: The Residential and Retail Energy Storage Market Acceleration Incentives Program provides financial incentives for the installation of new grid-connected distributed energy storage systems by participating contractors. Incentives are structured as fixed-rate incentives per kWh of system energy capacity and are available on a standard offer first-come, first-served basis. The Program includes market-rate incentives for residential and non-residential energy storage projects, along with higher incentives for energy storage projects serving disadvantaged communities.

records.title: Revolving Loan Fund
records.description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) requests applications from qualified contractors to utilize the Department of Energy - Energy Efficiency Revolving Loan Fund (DOE-EERLF) funds for projects financed by single family residential customers. NYSERDA has established a new revolving loan fund intended to spur investment in energy efficiency and decarbonization measures for single family residential housing. This program will offer low interest rate loans to low-to-moderate-income (LMI) single-family homeowners to complete energy efficiency retrofits. Four hundred thousand dollars ($400,000.00) per Qualified Applicant will be reserved to provide their eligible customers with low interest EERLF Loan (Loan).

records.title: Technical Skills Training and Upskilling
records.description: Funding is available to build and expand training capacity that advances skills and knowledge for clean energy workers in the areas of energy efficiency and building electrification, renewable energy, energy storage, smart grid, and electric vehicle charging stations. This solicitation may also support the enhancement of clean energy content delivered to students enrolled in a degree or certificate program at an accredited educational institution or an eligible career and technical education program. Funding is intended to minimize barriers to training by subsidizing the cost of training, making training more available across the state and ensuring that training is developed and delivered by qualified entities targeted at meeting demonstrated market gaps and needs.

records.title: The New York Truck-Voucher Incentive Program
records.description: Helps fleet owners in New York State afford clean vehicle technologies that are quiet, efficient and do not emit harmful pollutants or carbon. NYTVIP provides point-of-sale vouchers to fleet owners that purchase or lease zero emission Class 3-8 vehicles, non-road equipment, and transit buses. Information about how fleets, dealers, and manufacturers can participate in NYTVIP can be found in the Implementation Manual.

records.title: Window Heat Pump Demonstration Program - Phase I
records.description: NYSERDA’s Clean Heat for All: Packaged Window Heat Pump Demonstration Program provides up to $10 million in incentives to support the installation and performance monitoring of cold-climate packaged window heat pumps (PWHPs) in multifamily buildings across New York State. Through a two-phase structure, the Program qualifies manufacturers and vendors whose PWHP products meet technical and installation standards, and then provides cost-share incentives for demonstration projects that validate the products’ real-world performance. The program aims to accelerate adoption of PWHPs as an efficient, scalable retrofit solution and may inform future eligibility under the NYS Clean Heat program.

records.title: Window Heat Pump Demonstration Program - Phase II
records.description: NYSERDA’s Clean Heat for All: Packaged Window Heat Pump Demonstration Program provides up to $10 million in incentives to support the installation and performance monitoring of cold-climate packaged window heat pumps (PWHPs) in multifamily buildings across New York State. Through a two-phase structure, the Program qualifies manufacturers and vendors whose PWHP products meet technical and installation standards, and then provides cost-share incentives for demonstration projects that validate the products’ real-world performance. The program aims to accelerate adoption of PWHPs as an efficient, scalable retrofit solution and may inform future eligibility under the NYS Clean Heat program.

records.title: Clean Energy Financing Arrangements
records.description: NY Green Bank invites private sector capital providers and other clean energy industry participants to propose transactions involving NY Green Bank that facilitate the financing of clean energy projects in New York State, consistent with its mandate, mission and priorities in addressing financing market gaps and barriers.

records.title: Community Decarbonization Fund - Financing for Disadvantaged Community Lenders
records.description: NY Green Bank’s RFP 23 for the Community Decarbonization Fund invites regulated and unregulated financial entities (including but not limited to community development financial institutions (CDFIs), insured credit unions and depository institutions, and not-for-profit corporations that perform lending activities) deploying capital into clean energy and sustainable infrastructure and related small businesses that benefit disadvantaged communities (DACs) in New York State to submit proposals for NY Green Bank capital at concessionary rates.

records.title: Financing Arrangements for High-Performance Affordable Housing
records.description: NY Green Bank’s RFP 18 invites property owners and developers, energy service companies and equipment manufacturers, capital providers, and other market participants to submit proposals for NYGB investment in the construction or retrofit of multifamily affordable housing to high levels of energy performance in New York State.

records.title: Independent Internal Audit Services
records.description: Seeking proposals from qualified firms to provide independent internal audit, advisory, compliance, investigative, technology, cybersecurity, and related professional services to support NYSERDA’s Internal Audit function under a five-year umbrella contract.

records.title: Net-Zero Resilience Preparation for Municipal and Rural Electric Providers
records.description: Municipal electric utilities and rural electric cooperatives across New York State play a critical role in the areas they cover. The combined dynamics of a changing climate and the effects of decarbonization present a set of new operating considerations to continue to provide resilient and reliable services. Through RFP 6129, NYSERDA seeks to support the rapid decarbonization and increased resilience of municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives through demonstrations of Net Zero/Deep Decarbonization Solutions. Project proposers may include one or more electric municipal utilities or rural electric cooperatives. Entities other than a municipal utility or rural cooperative may apply on their behalf, provided that the proposal includes a letter of commitment from at least one New York State municipal utility or rural cooperative partner.

records.title: Port Infrastructure
records.description: Supporting maritime port development and improvement projects at existing New York State ports, NYSERDA seeks to competitively select and fund proposals through Request for Proposals (RFP) 6041. The program will invest in New York State’s existing ports to increase the capability for New York to support the offshore wind industry while also having multi-use purposes. Investing in ports capable of multi-purpose commercial activities ensures resiliency to demand fluctuations from any one market and subsequently provides job retention and job growth for New Yorkers. rnrnThe solicitation may have multiple rounds for proposal submission.rnrnThe due date for round 2 is 8/20/2026 at 3:00 PM ET.

records.title: Charge Ready NY 2.0 Equipment and Network Qualification Process
records.description: Establishes a list of Level 2 electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment and networks that will be eligible for incentives under the upcoming Charge Ready NY 2.0 Program. Under the Program, interested applicants will be able to receive incentives for the installation of eligible charging equipment. Charging station vendors will submit applications to determine eligibility of one or more models of charging equipment. Charging network operators will submit applications to have information about their network, and which eligible charging equipment it is compatible with, listed as part of program materials.

records.title: Clean Energy Training Services
records.description: NYSERDA is looking to establish a pool of contractors qualified to deliver training, develop curriculum and/or training tools, and provide market expertise and/or other services related to clean energy workforce development and training. Qualified contractors will have experience in one or more of the following categories: building decarbonization and energy efficiency, renewable energy, grid modernization and energy storage, alternative transportation, nuclear power, internship, mentorship, and leadership development, or labor relations. In addition, NYSERDA also seeks contractors with experience developing certifications/credentials and reaching underserved populations who encounter barriers to accessing training and jobs in the clean energy sector.

records.title: Disadvantaged Communities (DAC) Consultant Pool
records.close_date_note: Next of 5 future NYSERDA application rounds; later rounds are listed in the details.

deadlines.note: Next of 5 future NYSERDA application rounds; later rounds are listed in the details.

records.description: NYSERDA is seeking to expand the existing pool of qualified Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and other entities, including Indigenous Nations and Indigenous-led Organizations, that represent New York State’s disadvantaged communities (DAC), herein referred to “DAC Consultants.” DAC Consultants participating in this pool will execute contracts with NYSERDA to provide support across multiple programmatic areas, supporting teams with distinct, high-impact projects on an as needed basis.

records.title: Multifamily Contractor Network
records.description: Establishes a network of highly qualified firms who work directly with developers, building owners, and their representatives to plan and implement energy efficiency and beneficial electrification projects for Multifamily Residential programs.

records.title: New York State Flexible Energy Technical Analysis
records.description: Establishes a pool of consulting firms qualified to provide NYSERDA with diverse technical, energy, economic, and environmental analytical capacity, some of which may be requests for support services on short notice.

records.title: Upstate Through Wall Heat Pump Demonstration Program
records.description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) is seeking applications from owners, managers, or operators of multifamily buildings to serve as demonstration host sites for Packaged Terminal Heat Pumps (PTHPs) through the Clean Heat for All: Room Heat Pump Program. Eligible buildings must contain at least five (5) dwelling units, be located in New York State counties within climate zone 5 or 6, and have existing through-wall openings designed to house either standard PTACs, PTACs in hydronic cabinets or through-the-wall ACs.rnApproved applicants will join a qualified pool of demonstration host sites. Manufacturers selected under PON 5907 may partner with these building owners to plan and implement PTHP field demonstrations with installations expected to begin by the 2026 heating season (October/November 2026).
